items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: Oh, tell him the same for me.

ctx.x: people there. Oh, in those days there were relatively few Catholics there. That's right. That's right. Did they have any jazzy piano playing and jazzy music at the Protestant church you attended? No. Well I was raised up, for instance, going to both white churches and also Negro churches up there. They had some very gut-buckety piano playing, you know, rather goofy piano playing in the churches. There was one girl who, named Jewel Webb, who had learned it from listening to the records of the Economist who played…

Yeah, I forgot to tell you hello from below, Bonds. Remember the saxophone player which I left there? I met him on the street and he said to be sure and tell you hello. Oh, tell him the same for me. I will. I wanted to ask you about saxophone there. You remember him, huh? Yeah. Mealy Barnes, his little brother? His little brother, Mealy's little brother. But anyway, who was the first one to play a saxophone in New Orleans that you heard then?
Hmm. Oh, it's hard to say all now because it looked like when one picked it up the whole bunch started playing. Yeah.
